newsitem.title: CHINA: China land freeze not to hurt foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: China land freeze not to hurt foreign investors.

text.p: A one-year freeze imposed by China on the use of farmland for non-agricultural purposes will not affect foreign-funded projects, which will be encouraged to use idle land, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Large amounts of unused space in development zones as well as waste or barren land were available to foreign investors, who could also get Chinese partners to contribute land to projects, the official newspaper said.

"The freeze is not to hold up construction projects but to promote proper and efficient use of idle land," it quoted Pan Mingcai, director of the construction land department of the State Land Administration (SLA), as saying.
Projects that occupy farmland must get approval from the State Council, or cabinet, or wait for one year for the freeze to be lifted, Pan said.

The freeze is expected to force non-agricultural construction projects -- including foreign-funded ones -- to use alternatives, but would not apply to key State construction projects and an urban housing project, Pan said.
China is anxious to protect its precious farmland from development as the nation's economic boom drives up land prices.
About 466,000 hectares of farmland were occupied every year, but much was left unused, Pan said, adding that the problem was worst in some development zones.
